tools.name: meshy_text_to_3d

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. With model_type smart-topology: 'meshy-t2' (the default there) or 'meshy-t2.5' (newest, sharper detail for game assets).

model_type.description: standard (default); smart-topology (ai_model meshy-t2 or meshy-t2.5): a clean, part-separated, triangle-only mesh made directly at target_polycount, ignoring remesh/decimation. lowpoly (Meshy T1) is retired: use smart-topology with meshy-t2.5.

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default), 2k or 4k (finest); meshy-7.1/latest with model_type standard only, +5 credits.

target_polycount.description: Standard: remesh target 100–300,000, needs should_remesh true. Smart Topology: meshy-t2 100–15,000 (default 4,000), meshy-t2.5 100–30,000 (default 15,000).

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

tools.name: meshy_image_to_3d
tools.description:
Generate a 3D model from one image, textured by default (no refine step; should_texture false for a bare mesh). Typically 2–3 minutes.
Cost: meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 20 mesh only, 30 textured, 35 at 8K; meshy-6-lite 5 / 15; meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 5 / 15 / 20 at 8K; Ultra geometry +5.

IMAGE INPUT (exactly ONE):
  - file_path: a local image (RECOMMENDED; never base64-encode it yourself)
  - image_url: a public URL
  - input_task_id: a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image task with ONE image (multi-view output → meshy_multi_image_to_3d)

Example: { file_path: "/path/to/character.png", pose_mode: "t-pose" }

image_url.description: Public image URL. For local files use file_path.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp; the server encodes it.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task with exactly one image, used as the input.

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. With model_type smart-topology: 'meshy-t2' (the default there) or 'meshy-t2.5' (newest, sharper detail for game assets).

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default), 2k or 4k (finest); meshy-7.1/latest with model_type standard only, +5 credits.

model_type.description: standard (default); smart-topology (ai_model meshy-t2 or meshy-t2.5): a clean, part-separated, triangle-only mesh made directly at target_polycount, ignoring remesh/decimation. lowpoly (Meshy T1) is retired: use smart-topology with meshy-t2.5.

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

target_polycount.description: Standard: remesh target 100–300,000, needs should_remesh true. Smart Topology: meshy-t2 100–15,000 (default 4,000), meshy-t2.5 100–30,000 (default 15,000).

should_texture.description: Generate textures (default true); false gives a cheaper untextured mesh.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

image_enhancement.description: Optimize the input image (meshy-6/7.1/latest); false keeps deliberate styling.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only; API default true there).

save_pre_remeshed_model.description: Also keep the GLB from before remeshing (with should_remesh).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

tools.name: meshy_text_to_3d_refine
tools.description:
Texture a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_3d preview. Cost: 10 credits (15 at 8K). Get the user's approval first; omit ai_model to inherit the preview's model.

Example: { preview_task_id: "abc-123", texture_prompt: "rusty metal", enable_pbr: true }

preview_task_id.description: The SUCCEEDED preview task to texture

ai_model.description: Optional override: 'meshy-7.1', 'latest' (= 7.1), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (2K only). Omit (recommended) to inherit the preview's model; not meshy-t2/t2.5.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only). Sent as-is when ai_model is omitted, so omit it after a meshy-6-lite preview (the API rejects it).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

tools.name: meshy_multi_image_to_3d
tools.description:
Generate a 3D model from 1–4 views of the same object (better reconstruction), textured by default.
Cost: meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 20 mesh only, 30 textured, 35 at 8K; meshy-6-lite 5 / 15; Ultra geometry +5.

IMAGE INPUT (exactly ONE):
  - file_paths: 1–4 local images (never base64-encode them yourself)
  - image_urls: 1–4 public URLs
  - input_task_id: a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image task (multi-view included); its images are the input

Example: { file_paths: ["/path/front.jpg", "/path/side.jpg"] }

file_paths.description: 1–4 absolute paths to local .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp images; the server encodes them.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task (multi-view included) whose images are the input.

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. No Smart Topology here.

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default) or 2k (+5 credits); meshy-7.1/latest only. No 4k here.

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

model_type.description: Deprecated; ignored (this endpoint has no model_type).

should_texture.description: Generate textures (default true); false gives a cheaper untextured mesh.

texture_image_urls.description: 1–4 views (URLs or data URIs) of the SAME object to drive the texture; element 0 is the front. meshy-7.1/latest only; not with texture_prompt / texture_image_url.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

image_enhancement.description: Optimize the input image (meshy-6/7.1/latest); false keeps deliberate styling.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6/7.1/latest; API default true).

save_pre_remeshed_model.description: Also keep the GLB from before remeshing (with should_remesh).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

tools.name: meshy_get_task_status
tools.description:
Wait for a task to finish (wait=true, default) or check it once (wait=false). Reports the task's real task_type; pass it to the download and cancel tools.

wait=true polls at the API's suggested interval (else 5s→30s backoff) until SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED or timeout_seconds runs out; a failed status check (timeout, 429, 5xx) is retried at the next poll. Running out of time returns outcome "TIMEOUT": the task keeps running on Meshy — call again with the same task_id (Meshy advises allowing up to 60 minutes from creation).

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

wait.description: true (default): poll until it finishes; false: return the current status.

timeout_seconds.description: Max wait for this call when wait=true; the task keeps running after it.

tools.name: meshy_list_tasks
tools.description:
List tasks of any status, newest first by default, merged across the types queried (one request per type). Default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image and image-to-image; pass task_type / task_types for printing, rigging, animation, motion, post-processing or Creative Lab tasks. With a task_id in hand, use meshy_get_task_status instead. Tasks created through the API do not appear in the Meshy web app.

status and phase filter the fetched tasks, so a page can be shorter than limit; continue with next_offset while has_more. Types whose request failed are listed in failed_types. For finished 3D models only, meshy_list_models is cheaper.

task_type.description: One task type to list (same names as meshy_get_task_status).

task_types.description: Task types to list, merged with task_type. Default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image.

tools.name: meshy_cancel_task
tools.description:
Cancel a queued task, or delete a finished one. What happens depends on the task:

Creative Lab tasks (task_type "creative-lab-..."):
  - PENDING → canceled, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → canceled, credits NOT refunded
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → cannot be canceled or deleted, even with confirm_delete

Every other task:
  - PENDING → deleted, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → refused: the task keeps running and its credits are not refundable. Wait until it finishes
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → PERMANENTLY deleted with its files, no refund. Requires confirm_delete: true — ask the user first

Returns { success, task_id, task_type, previous_status, message }.

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

confirm_delete.description: true to permanently delete a finished task, only after the user agreed.

tools.name: meshy_download_model
tools.description:
Save a finished task's output under meshy_output/ (project folders with history), or at save_to.

  - 3D tasks: ONE model format — ask the user which first (GLB viewing, OBJ white-model printing, 3MF multicolor printing, FBX game engines, USDZ AR, BLEND Blender); never download all. A format exists only if it was generated: 3mf needs target_formats ["3mf"] at creation, meshy_convert or meshy_process_multicolor.
  - Creative Lab: omit format to save every part.
  - Images and text-to-motion clips save their own files and ignore format.
  - Rigging and animation tasks are not saved: they return their file URLs.
If a download fails, its URL is returned instead.

Example (print): { task_id: "abc-123", format: "obj", print_ready: true, print_height_mm: 100 }

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

format.description: Model format (default glb; omit for every Creative Lab part).

save_to.description: Absolute file path to save to instead of meshy_output/{timestamp}_{prompt}_{id}/

parent_task_id.description: Earlier task of the same chain (e.g. the preview of a refine); saves into its project folder.

print_ready.description: OBJ only: rotate Y-up to Z-up, scale to print_height_mm, center, bottom at Z=0. Changes only the local file (free); meshy_resize (1 credit) rescales the model on Meshy.

print_height_mm.description: Height in mm with print_ready (default 75; '15 cm' → 150).

tools.name: meshy_list_models
tools.description: List your finished 3D models (not AI models), newest first, each with its task_id, task_type and formats ready for meshy_download_model. Queries only image-to-3d by default (one request); pass task_types to widen. meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status instead, images included.

task_types.description: Model task types to list (default ["image-to-3d"], one request). Pass several, e.g. ["text-to-3d", "image-to-3d", "multi-image-to-3d"], to widen; each type is one more request.

tools.name: meshy_remesh
tools.description:
Remesh an existing model: change its polygon count or topology. Cost: 5 credits. For a format change only use meshy_convert (1 credit); to scale, meshy_resize (1 credit).

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", topology: "quad", target_polycount: 10000, target_formats: ["fbx"] }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d (preview or refine), image-to-3d or retexture task

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

tools.name: meshy_retexture
tools.description:
Apply new AI textures to an existing model. Cost: 10 credits (15 at 8K).

Ask the user for EXACTLY ONE style input (the tool rejects combinations):
  - text_style_prompt: the style in words ("rusty metal", "cartoon")
  - image_style_url: one image used as a STYLE reference
  - multiview_image_urls: 1–4 photos OF THE SAME OBJECT from different angles (not style references)

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", text_style_prompt: "rusty metal" }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d (preview or refine), image-to-3d or remesh task

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

text_style_prompt.description: The texture style in words (max 800 characters).

image_style_url.description: One image used as the style reference.

multiview_image_urls.description: 1–4 ordered views of the same object; element 0 is primary and alone drives metallic/roughness. Needs Meshy 7 ('latest' is sent as 'meshy-7').

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7), 'meshy-7', 'meshy-6', or 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, 2K only). No meshy-7.1 here.

enable_original_uv.description: Keep the existing UVs instead of a fresh unwrap. Default true with input_task_id, false with model_url (safest for uploads).

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (15 credits instead of 10; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only; API default true there).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it).

tools.name: meshy_rig
tools.description:
Auto-rig a humanoid character for animation. Cost: 5 credits, including free walking + running animations (GLB + FBX, separate files).

REQUIREMENT: a textured humanoid (biped) model with a clear body and limbs, ≤300,000 faces (checked first; remesh if over). model_url must be a .glb facing +Z. Generate characters with pose_mode "t-pose" for the best rig.

Next steps: meshy_download_model (task_type "rigging") returns the rigged model and walk/run URLs. Other actions: meshy_list_animations → meshy_animate. A described motion: meshy_text_to_motion → meshy_animate with motion_task_id.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a textured humanoid model

model_url.description: Public URL of a textured humanoid .glb (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

height_meters.description: Character height in meters; helps scaling

texture_image_url.description: Deprecated: leave it out when the model has its own textures (Meshy models and most GLBs do), which the rig keeps. Sending it makes this image the only texture and drops the PBR maps. Only for a model_url GLB without textures: its UV-unwrapped base color (.png, max 20 MB)

tools.name: meshy_animate

action_id.description: One preset action; find ids with meshy_list_animations (free), never guess.

action_ids.description: 1–10 unique preset ids, returned as ONE file with one clip per action, in this order (e.g. for a game-engine state machine).

motion_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_motion task (biped rigs only; within 3 days, before the clip expires).

tools.name: meshy_text_to_motion

prompt.description: The motion, e.g. 'jumps over a gap and lands in a crouch' (max 400 characters).

duration.description: Clip length in seconds: 2–10 in steps of 0.5.

mode.description: 'prime' (default): highest quality, FBX. 'swift': faster and cheaper, BVH.

tools.name: meshy_list_animations
tools.description:
Look up preset animations: the action ids meshy_animate takes. Free. Filters combine; with none the whole (long) library comes back, so prefer search or category.

Returns [{ action_id, name, key, category, sub_category, preview_url }]; preview_url is an animated GIF.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of the animation name or key, e.g. 'walk', 'punch', 'dance'.

sub_category.description: Only this sub-category, e.g. 'AttackingwithWeapon'. Names repeat across categories, so pair it with category to be exact.

action_ids.description: Resolve these ids (up to 200); ids that no longer exist are simply absent.

tools.name: meshy_convert
tools.description:
Convert a model to other file formats. Cost: 1 credit (cheaper than remesh for a format-only change).

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", target_formats: ["stl", "3mf"] }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a model. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

tools.name: meshy_resize

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a model (output GLB). Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (output keeps its format), or a GLB data URI.

resize_longest_side.description: Longest side in meters (aspect ratio kept)

tools.name: meshy_uv_unwrap
tools.description:
Make a clean, non-overlapping UV layout ("UV white model") before texturing in Blender, Substance Painter or Unreal. Cost: 5 credits.

GLB input only, ≤40,000 faces (denser meshes are rejected: remesh first). The output GLB keeps the geometry (quads/n-gons triangulated) with fresh UVs and a grey placeholder material.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a GLB. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL or data URI of a .glb (convert other formats first).

tools.name: meshy_text_to_image
tools.description:
Generate a 2D image from text, e.g. a design for the user to approve before 3D. Typically ~30 s.
Cost: nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9, GPT Image models 9 credits.

To make it 3D: meshy_image_to_3d with input_task_id = this task (multi-view output: meshy_multi_image_to_3d).

Example: { ai_model: "nano-banana-pro", prompt: "game character", generate_multi_view: true, pose_mode: "t-pose" }

generate_multi_view.description: Front/side/back views (input for meshy_multi_image_to_3d). Not with aspect_ratio.

aspect_ratio.description: Default '1:1'; '3:2' and '2:3' are GPT Image models only. Not with generate_multi_view.

remove_background.description: Transparent-background PNG (no effect on multi-view output).

tools.name: meshy_image_to_image
tools.description:
Edit or restyle images with a text prompt. Cost: nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9, GPT Image models 12 credits.
Give exactly ONE reference source: input_task_id (all images of an earlier image task), reference_file_paths (local files; never base64-encode them yourself) or reference_image_urls.

To make the result 3D: meshy_image_to_3d with input_task_id = this task (multi-view output: meshy_multi_image_to_3d).

Example: { ai_model: "nano-banana-2", prompt: "make it red", input_task_id: "abc-123" }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task; all its images are the references. Wins over the other sources.

reference_file_paths.description: 1–5 absolute paths to local images; the server encodes them

generate_multi_view.description: Front/side/back views (input for meshy_multi_image_to_3d). Not with aspect_ratio.

aspect_ratio.description: Default '1:1'; '3:2' and '2:3' are GPT Image models only. Not with generate_multi_view.

remove_background.description: Transparent-background PNG (no effect on multi-view output).

tools.name: meshy_send_to_slicer
tools.description:
Detect installed 3D printing slicers and return their launch commands. Call it at the START of a print workflow and keep the result; at the END, replace {file} in a launch_command with the downloaded file's local path and run it. If you cannot run shell commands, give the user the command and the file path.

Detects OrcaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Creality Print, Elegoo Slicer, Anycubic Slicer Next, PrusaSlicer (all multicolor-capable) and UltiMaker Cura.

Several SEPARATE models: open them one at a time, ~2 s apart (`open -a "Bambu Studio" a.stl; sleep 2; open -a "Bambu Studio" b.stl`); fired together, a slicer may take only one. Parts of one model go in one project, opened together.

model_url.description: The model's URL (a placeholder is fine when only detecting)

slicer_type.description: 'auto' (default): detect all and recommend one; or one slicer.

tools.name: meshy_analyze_printability
tools.description:
Check whether a model is printable: watertightness, non-manifold edges, holes, degenerate faces and volume — plus thin walls when printer_type and/or a print size is given (FDM, SLA/resin or full-color). FREE. This is the authoritative answer to "is it printable?".

The finished task (task_type "print-analyze") reports printability.status:
  - error → meshy_repair_printability (pass this analyze task as input_task_id to reuse its printer and size)
  - warning → repair is optional
  - healthy → download the analyzed source task's model (the analyze task has none)

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", printer_type: "sla", intended_print_height_mm: 100 }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, remesh or retexture task on Meshy 6 or newer, or a print-repair task. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

printer_type.description: Sets the minimum wall: fdm 1.0 mm, sla 0.8 mm, full_color 2.0 mm (fdm when only a size is sent). Without a size: 150 mm tall for GLB / tasks, an STL's own size, else 150 mm longest side.

intended_print_height_mm.description: Print height in mm (1–1000); GLB / input_task_id only. At most one print size.

intended_print_longest_side_mm.description: Print's longest side in mm (1–1000); any format. At most one print size.

tools.name: meshy_repair_printability
tools.description:
Repair a model for 3D printing (FDM, SLA/resin or full-color): fixes non-manifold edges, degenerate faces and holes and makes it watertight. Cost: 10 credits. Textures are removed (retexture afterwards if needed).

Output format: input_task_id → GLB; model_url → the input's format (.stl → STL, .obj → OBJ…). To keep a Meshy model as OBJ, pass its OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) as model_url.
With printer_type and/or a print size it also thickens walls that are too thin, when over 5% of the surface is. The model keeps its scale (meshy_resize scales it).

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, remesh or retexture task, or a print-analyze task (which passes on its printer and size). Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

printer_type.description: Sets the minimum wall: fdm 1.0 mm, sla 0.8 mm, full_color 2.0 mm (fdm when only a size is sent). Without a size: 150 mm tall for GLB / tasks, an STL's own size, else 150 mm longest side.

intended_print_height_mm.description: Print height in mm (1–1000); GLB / input_task_id only. At most one print size.

intended_print_longest_side_mm.description: Print's longest side in mm (1–1000); any format. At most one print size.

tools.name: meshy_process_multicolor
tools.description:
Turn a textured model into a multi-color 3MF that opens ready to print in the slicer of printer_brand. Cost: 10 credits.

Confirm first: max_colors (the printer's AMS/MMU capacity), style, printer_brand, and max_depth (realistic only).
Download with format "3mf", then open it with meshy_send_to_slicer (is_multicolor). Flashforge, QIDI, Snapmaker and AnkerMake slicers are not detected: give the user the 3MF path for that slicer.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED textured task: image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d (unless should_texture was false), refined text-to-3d, remesh or retexture. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a textured .glb / .fbx, or a GLB data URI.

max_colors.description: Palette size (1–16); match the printer's AMS/MMU capacity.

max_depth.description: 3–6: higher = finer color boundaries, larger file (realistic only).

style.description: 'realistic' (default): photo-like detail, larger file, needs one base color texture with UVs on every part. 'cartoon': flat regions, smaller file, also takes vertex colors.

printer_brand.description: Brand whose slicer preset (default printer, 0.4 mm nozzle) goes into the 3MF (default bambu).

tools.name: meshy_auto_split
tools.description:
Cut a model into separately printable parts: when it is too big for the bed, parts need different colors/materials, or it should be assembled. Cost: 10 credits. The texture is not kept.

There is no bed-size parameter: cuts follow mode and prompt, not your printer, so resize the model to the print size first (meshy_resize) when parts must fit a bed, then check the part sizes and re-split by_parts if one is still too big.
Then meshy_download_model (3mf if requested) and meshy_send_to_slicer.

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", mode: "by_parts", prompt: "the figure and the base", target_formats: ["3mf"], connectors: true }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-3d preview, remesh, convert or resize task made with meshy-6, meshy-7, meshy-7.1 or latest (not low-poly or Smart Topology).

mode.description: 'auto' (default; Meshy picks the cuts), 'by_parts' (the parts named in prompt), or 'by_color' (the color regions named in prompt; image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d sources only).

prompt.description: Required for by_parts / by_color: name 1–10 parts, e.g. 'head, torso, arms, legs'; the rest becomes one more part. If unreadable, the task falls back to auto, still charges, and reports prompt_ignored.

target_formats.description: Extra formats (glb is always made). 3mf gives separately selectable parts in a slicer; stl fuses them into one solid.

layout.description: 'assembled' (default) or 'on_plate' (parts laid flat, ready to slice).

connectors.description: Add mortise-and-tenon connectors at each cut so the parts fit together.

tools.name: meshy_creative_lab
tools.description:
Turn a photo (file_path or image_url; no text prompt) into a finished Creative Lab product 3D model, end to end.

Products and cost — confirm before calling:
  - figure (chibi), vinyl-figure, brick-figure, keychain, fridge-magnet, fidget-pixel (pixel-art board of interlocking pieces) → 36 credits (6 + 30)
  - lamp (3D-printable lampshade with base plate) → 36 (30 + 6)
  - keycap (Cherry MX 1u) → 62 (12 + 50)
  - fidget-collapsible (nested-ring fidget from the photo's outline) → 6, one stage

Most products run a concept prototype, then a 3D build. One call runs both, blocks while they run (typically 2–5 minutes, with progress) and returns only the final model; the concept image is internal and never shown. If the prototype does not succeed, the build is NOT started: a FAILED stage is refunded; one still running when the wait ends keeps running and is charged.

Outputs: GLB (or output_format) for figures, keychain and fridge-magnet; lamp_stl (+ base_stl with a fixture preset); keycap a model; fidget-pixel a 3MF with one object per piece; fidget-collapsible STL + GLB. Download with meshy_download_model and the task_type this tool reports; omit format to save every part.
To multicolor-print it, pass its GLB URL (or a GLB data URI) to meshy_process_multicolor as model_url; its task id is not accepted there.

Examples:
  - { product: "keychain", file_path: "/Users/me/dog.jpg", name_text: "Biscuit", build_options: { badge_shape: "star" } }
  - { product: "fidget-pixel", file_path: "/Users/me/cat.jpg", pixel_subject: "other", build_options: { grid_size: 16 } }

product.description: The product (see the tool description for costs).

image_url.description: Public URL or data URI of the photo (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp). For local files use file_path.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local photo; the server encodes it.

image_subject.description: Lamp only: what the photo shows.

pixel_subject.description: fidget-pixel only, REQUIRED: 'person' → chibi pixel sprite; 'other' (pets, objects, logos, landscapes) → bead-art icon.

name_text.description: Keychain only: text to engrave, ≤10 characters (CJK count one each).

head_size_mm.description: Keycap only: the head's LONGEST edge in mm (default 23), not its height.

vertical_offset_mm.description: Keycap only: raise (+) or lower (-) the head on the base, in mm (default 0).

build_options.description: Build options (the API checks ranges). Keychain / fridge-magnet: badge_shape (circle|rounded-rect|hexagon|shield|star), size_mm, relief_height_mm, relief_offset_mm, base_thickness_mm, has_closed_back, relief_curve (linear|gamma|s-curve), curve_param, invert_depth, smoothing, relief_scale, depth_threshold, remove_background, export_resolution. Lamp: diameter_mm (50–400), thickness_mm, cut_amount_percent, light_source_preset (bambu_mh001_60mm|none), fixture_offset_x_mm, fixture_offset_z_mm, rotate_x_deg, rotate_y_deg, rotate_z_deg, include_result_json. Fidget pixel: shape (square|hex), grid_size (16|32), piece_size_mm (6|8|10; hex 6|8), color_count (1–8), piece_height_mm (10–80). Other products take none.

output_format.description: Keychain / fridge-magnet: glb (default), obj (zip of OBJ + MTL + texture) or zip (everything). Lamp: stl (default) or zip. Fidget pixel: 3mf. Others: none.

name.description: Display name for the task; not engraved (see name_text).

timeout_seconds.description: Max wait per stage in seconds; a longer stage keeps running (check it with meshy_get_task_status).

tools.name: meshy_check_balance
tools.description: Check the Meshy credit balance. Free. For team members it is the team's shared pool.

tools.name: meshy_list_usage

start_time.description: RFC 3339 start of the created_at window (default: 30 days before end_time; at most 1 year).

end_time.description: RFC 3339 end of the window (default now).

endpoints.description: Only these endpoints ('text-to-3d' covers preview and refine). Omit for all.

status.description: Only tasks with this final status. Omit for both.

instructions:
# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)
6. Present slicer list from step 1, ask user which to use, run its launch_command
If the model must be printed in pieces (too big for the bed, separate colors or materials), use Scenario L.

## Scenario B: 3D Printing (multicolor)
Trigger: user wants multicolor/color print.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect multicolor-capable slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, is_multicolor:true) — present list, save for later
2. Generate a textured model — image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d (textured by default), or text-to-3d preview + refine
3. meshy_process_multicolor with input_task_id of the textured task (confirm its options)
4. Wait, then download with format "3mf"
5. Present slicer list from step 1, ask user which to use, run its launch_command

## Scenario C: Game Engine (Unity/Unreal/Godot)
Trigger: user mentions game, Unity, Unreal, Godot, game-ready.
Suggested flow:
1. Generate model with target_formats:["fbx"]
2. Textures: image-to-3d / multi-image output is already textured (unless should_texture:false); a text-to-3d preview needs meshy_text_to_3d_refine
3. Inspect topology and face count. Smart Topology may already meet the budget; remesh only if needed and separately approved
4. Download FBX

## Scenario D: Character Animation
Trigger: user mentions rig, animate, walking, running, character animation.
Suggested flow:
1. Generate model with pose_mode:"t-pose"
2. Textures (rigging needs a textured humanoid): image-to-3d / multi-image output is already textured (unless should_texture:false); a text-to-3d preview needs meshy_text_to_3d_refine
3. Rig the model (meshy_rig, ≤300K faces; if over, remesh to reduce polycount first)
4. Download — rigging includes walking+running free, as separate files. For other actions use meshy_animate:
   - preset actions: look up action ids with meshy_list_animations (free) — never guess ids. action_ids puts up to 10 clips in one file (include the walk/run ids to bundle them too)
   - a described motion ("a backflip into a crouch"): meshy_text_to_motion, then meshy_animate with motion_task_id (biped rigs only)

## Scenario E: AR / Apple
Trigger: user mentions AR, USDZ, Vision Pro, Quick Look.
Suggested flow:
1. Generate model with target_formats:["usdz"]
2. Textures: image-to-3d / multi-image output is already textured (unless should_texture:false); a text-to-3d preview needs meshy_text_to_3d_refine
3. If the model has no USDZ yet, convert it (meshy_convert, target_formats:["usdz"])
4. Download USDZ

## Scenario F: Retexture
Trigger: user wants to change textures/style of existing model.
Suggested flow:
1. Ask the user for EXACTLY ONE style input (see meshy_retexture), then call it.

## Scenario H: Cheap Format Conversion / Resize
Trigger: user has an existing model (task or URL) and only needs another file format, or wants it scaled to real-world dimensions — no re-generation.
Suggested flow:
1. Format only → meshy_convert (supports 3mf; cheaper than remesh).
2. Real-world size → meshy_resize.
3. Wait, then meshy_download_model.

## Scenario I: UV Unwrap (before external texturing)
Trigger: user wants to texture a model in Blender / Substance Painter / Unreal, or needs a clean UV layout / "UV white model".
Suggested flow:
1. The source must be a GLB with ≤40,000 faces — if denser, meshy_remesh to a lower target_polycount first.
2. meshy_uv_unwrap, wait, then meshy_download_model (format "glb").

## Scenario J: Creative Lab Consumer Products
Trigger: user wants a stylized physical-product model from a photo — chibi / vinyl / brick figure, keychain, fridge magnet, keycap, lamp, pixel-art or collapsible fidget.
Suggested flow:
1. Confirm the product, its cost and options (see meshy_creative_lab), then call it once with a photo.
2. Download with the task_type it reports; omit format to save every part.

## Scenario K: Cleaner Topology / Part-Separated Geometry (cheaply)
Trigger: user wants an editable, part-separated, or lower-poly model from an image or text.
Suggested flow:
1. Confirm the model (meshy-t2, or meshy-t2.5: newest, sharper detail for game assets), cost, face target, and whether textures are wanted.
2. Call meshy_image_to_3d or meshy_text_to_3d with model_type:"smart-topology", that ai_model, and target_polycount. Set should_texture false on the image route when only geometry is approved.
3. Text preview is untextured; confirm refine separately, without a refine ai_model override.

## Scenario L: Print in Parts (Auto Split)
Trigger: model is too big for the print bed, or parts should be printed separately / in different colors and assembled.
Suggested flow:
1. Check the source qualifies (see meshy_auto_split).
2. Confirm the cost and how to cut: mode "auto", "by_parts" with a prompt naming 1–10 parts, or "by_color" (image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d sources only). There is no bed-size parameter: resize to the print size first if parts must fit a bed, then check part sizes and re-split by_parts if one is still too big. Offer connectors so the pieces fit together, layout "on_plate" for print-ready placement, and target_formats ["3mf"] for separately selectable parts in a slicer.
3. meshy_auto_split, wait, meshy_download_model, then open the file in a slicer (meshy_send_to_slicer).

## Scenario G: General 3D Model (default)
Trigger: none of the above.
Suggested flow:
1. Ask user about intended use to determine format
2. From text, offer the image route (meshy_text_to_image → user approves the image → meshy_image_to_3d with input_task_id; textured in one task), or a quick meshy_text_to_3d preview (+ meshy_text_to_3d_refine for textures)
3. Download in chosen format
